task: Find a FREE sub-hourly historical surface-obs feed for EGLC (London City Airport), the exact station Polymarket's London high-temp ladder settles on (per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md, wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC).
verdict_tier: sub-hourly, MARGINAL tier per task rubric (30-min, not 10-min-or-better)
headline: EGLC issues genuine half-hourly (H:20 and H:50 UTC) automated METAR/SPECI reports, not just hourly. Verified via three independent free sources (IEM global ASOS mirror, NOAA aviationweather.gov, Ogimet) with exact-match cross-checked values. This is 2x the obs density (48 obs/day) that the prior repo study (ref/pmkt_final_verdict.py, which queried IEM with report_type=3 only) assumed (24-25 obs/day, 'routine hourly METAR'). No auth, no rate-limit gate, >=164 days of retrievable history confirmed (likely years more, not exhaustively tested). Does NOT reach the 10-min/100-rows-per-day 'strongly preferred' tier -- no genuinely finer (10-min or better) free station feed for EGLC was found; UK Met Office's own official channels (DataHub, MIDAS Open) are either auth/paid-plan-gated or hourly-only.

candidates_checked.name: UK Met Office Weather DataHub (site-specific observations)
candidates_checked.status: CHECKED, NOT VIABLE for this task
candidates_checked.reason: DataPoint (the old free/open service) was retired in 2025 with 'no like-for-like replacement service for the UK site-specific observation data.' The successor DataHub requires creating a Met Office DataHub account and subscribing to a 'Site Specific' Global Spot plan (free tier exists for low volume, but is account/API-key gated, not anonymous-open) -- and public docs describe forecast/current-obs products, not a confirmed sub-hourly HISTORICAL archive. Not pulled live (would need account creation, out of scope for a same-session free-feed verification); flagged as a dead end for now, not fully exhaustively tested.

auth_summary: No API key, no account, no login required for the winning feed (IEM asos.py) or its two cross-check sources (aviationweather.gov, Ogimet single-hour query). All three are anonymous HTTP GET.
rate_limits_summary: No documented hard rate limit found for any of the three sources used. This session made ~7 sequential GET requests across IEM/aviationweather.gov/Ogimet at roughly 1/sec with pauses, no throttling, no errors, no CAPTCHA. Continued politeness (sequential, ~1 req/sec, cache-then-reuse) recommended per GROUNDING.md non-negotiable #8.
licensing_summary: IEM: public redistribution of WMO GTS METAR traffic, no restrictive terms found on the request endpoint. Ogimet: states free for non-commercial/research use. aviationweather.gov: US government (NOAA) public data, no restriction. None of these are the UK Met Office's own data product, but all three ultimately carry the same underlying EGLC-originated METAR/SPECI report -- the same station and same report family Polymarket's Wunderground settlement page itself scrapes, per ref/pmkt_settlement_basis.md's 100% (14/14) IEM-vs-settled agreement finding for London.
relevance_to_grounding_blocker: ref/GROUNDING.md and ref/pmkt_final_verdict.md's STILL-BLOCKED verdict cite 'hourly METAR... under-reports the diurnal peak by ~1h of temperature change' as the coverage blocker for the 5 non-US whitelist cities including London. This feedhunt found that EGLC specifically is NOT limited to hourly cadence on this same free IEM source -- the prior script's report_type=3-only query call undercounted it. Re-running the coverage/signal-fire analysis for London with the corrected report_type=3&4 (30-min) pull is a natural, cheap next step that could partially narrow (not necessarily close) the 74% no-signal-fired gap for this one city -- flagged for a follow-up study, not claimed as resolved here.
